node.label: Robert Darnton
node.date_label: The Literary Underground of the Old Regime (1982) · The Great Cat Massacre (1984) · The Forbidden Best-Sellers of Pre-Revolutionary France (1995)
node.description: Historian of books and eighteenth-century French culture who connects the production and circulation of texts with readers’ meanings. Carla Hesse’s1999 account explains how archives of publishing and clandestine literature intersected with Darnton’s collaboration with Clifford Geertz. His anthropological interpretations remain readings of situated symbolic practices; the archive does not give unmediated access to every reader or a single cause of revolution.

named_group_routes.relationship: Geertz’s interpretation of symbolic practices becomes a resource for cultural history
named_group_routes.evidence_note: Hunt’s primary 1984 p. 87 supplies a named reception example; the existing political-history edge specifies that use. Darnton’s original acknowledgments add a specific Princeton co-teaching mechanism with Geertz; his introduction names Lévi-Strauss and acknowledges archival mediation. Davis (revision 1.143): she acknowledged reading Geertz ‘eclectically’ among other anthropologists and co-teaching a course with him at Princeton (Haskins Lecture, 1997, pp. 14, 19, read in full); the checked passages establish no specific adoption of thick description, and her anthropological route is recorded on the anthropology → natalie_zemon_davis edge. None of this certifies all anthropological routes into cultural history. Earlier review (to revision 1.142): Davis was recorded as ‘an earlier proposed example whose direct reception is not established by the passages checked here’.

named_group_routes.relationship: Bourdieu’s distinction between practical sense and scholastic reason (cited 2003) and his account of social difference (2007 dialogue); Certeau restored the space of readers’ appropriation, though Chartier rejects reading his “poaching” as absolute freedom
named_group_routes.evidence_note: His own words. 2003 article, read in full: to think "cette irréductibilité de l'expérience au discours", historians could rely on Foucault's distinction and on "celle établie par Bourdieu entre « sens pratique » et « raison scolastique »" (¶25, n. 26: Méditations pascaliennes, 1997). 2007 dialogue with Darnton, read in part in Portuguese translation (MATRIZes 5:2, 2012): social difference "não decorre apenas dessa tradição da história social da Annales, decorre também … ao trabalho de Pierre Bourdieu" (p. 164); no contradiction between Bourdieu's sociology of cultural production and McKenzie's sociology of texts (p. 166); "De Certeau, entre outros, restituiu este espaço" between constraints and readers' appropriation, but "seria um erro acreditar que esta liberdade é absoluta" (p. 167). In 1988 he recorded five radio dialogues with Bourdieu, published as a book in 2010 (presentation, p. 162; Prismas bibliography). Named resources with qualifications, not adherence to a school.

named_group_routes.relationship: Later studies of the mobility of texts across attributions, printed versions, forms of publication, genres and translations: the lost Cardenio between Cervantes and Shakespeare (2011) and Éditer et traduire (2021), in their reviewers’ accounts
named_group_routes.evidence_note: Mediated: the books are unread. Boucheron's review of Cardenio (Books & Ideas, 2014; consulted through WebFetch extraction; selected quoted passages recorded; full text not collated): its problem is "the discrepancy between the mobility of texts and the stability of authorial names"; Boucheron expects the claim that the author function took its final form in the eighteenth century to "provoke debate, particularly among Medievalists": an anticipated objection, not a later controversy investigated here. Jouhaud (Prismas 26, 2022, pp. 236–237, read) quotes Éditer et traduire on "las cinco modalidades que suministran a las obras su movilidad" (attribution, printed variants, forms of publication, genres, translation). Chartier's own 2020–2021 Collège de France report (read via WebFetch extraction) describes research "vouées à comprendre les raisons de la mobilité des textes". Prismas's bibliography dates the books (2011; 2021). A contribution to the history of publishing and circulation within intellectual history; Darnton's separate strand membership is unchanged.

verification.note: Consulted through WebFetch extraction for revision 1.147; selected quoted passages recorded; full text not collated (no pagination). The book "adopts the style and format of an investigation" and opens with the court performance of winter 1612–1613; its problem is "the discrepancy between the mobility of texts and the stability of authorial names"; Theobald's Double Falshood (1727) is examined as possibly the "only surviving textual trace"; Boucheron reports Chartier's view that the Foucauldian author function reached its "final form" in the eighteenth century and adds that "This assertion will undoubtedly provoke debate, particularly among Medievalists" (an anticipated objection); "an historical essay that is in many respects experimental". The book itself is unread.

sources.title: “Roger Chartier entrevistado por Robert Darnton,” transcription and Portuguese translation by Dorothée de Bruchard, presentation and notes by Sandra Reimão, MATRIZes 5, no. 2 (2012): 159–177.
sources.citation: “Roger Chartier entrevistado por Robert Darnton,” transcription and Portuguese translation by Dorothée de Bruchard, presentation and notes by Sandra Reimão, MATRIZes 5, no. 2 (2012): 159–177.

verification.note: Read in part for revision 1.147 (open-access PDF from the USP journal): presentation pp. 159–162 and Darnton's questions II–IV with Chartier's answers, pp. 164–167, in Portuguese translation; p. 163 (the first question and answer) is not cited. Page layout rechecked in the journal PDF on 2026-10-19. The dialogue took place at the Collège de France on the occasion of the October 2007 inaugural lecture; its exact date is not given. Presentation: debts to Martin, McKenzie and Petrucci (pp. 159–160); in 1988 Chartier recorded five radio interviews with Bourdieu, published by the INA in 1988, and the 2010 book Le sociologue et l'historien (p. 162). Chartier: social difference "não decorre apenas dessa tradição da história social da Annales, decorre também … ao trabalho de Pierre Bourdieu" (p. 164); "pode-se considerar as diferenças entre os sexos como uma diferença social" (p. 164); no "relações imediatas, mecânicas, entre meios sociais e práticas culturais" (p. 165); no contradiction between Bourdieu's sociology of cultural production and McKenzie's sociology of texts (p. 166); between determinism of form and the reader's absolute freedom, "limitação transgredida e liberdade cerceada"; "De Certeau, entre outros, restituiu este espaço" between constraints and readers' appropriation, but "seria um erro acreditar que esta liberdade é absoluta", an "uso infeliz" of the essay on reading as poaching (p. 167).

sources.title: Christian Jouhaud, “Al pie del acantilado,” trans. Lucía Vogelfang, Prismas: Revista de historia intelectual 26 (2022): 235–240 (dossier “Roger Chartier y las migraciones históricas de la cultura escrita”).
sources.citation: Christian Jouhaud, “Al pie del acantilado,” trans. Lucía Vogelfang, Prismas: Revista de historia intelectual 26 (2022): 235–240 (dossier “Roger Chartier y las migraciones históricas de la cultura escrita”).

verification.note: Read in part for revision 1.147 (open-access PDF, pp. 235–237). Jouhaud describes "una obra caracterizada por su fuerte coherencia y por su impresionante energía historiográfica" since Lectures et lecteurs (p. 236); quotes Au bord de la falaise (1998, p. 269) on the essential object of literary history and textual criticism as "el proceso a través del cual lectores, espectadores u oyentes dan sentido a los textos que se apropian" (pp. 235–236); and quotes Éditer et traduire (2021) on "las cinco modalidades que suministran a las obras su movilidad: la inestabilidad de su atribución, las variaciones entre los textos respecto de sus versiones impresas, la pluralidad de sus formas de publicación, sus migraciones entre géneros y sus traducciones de un idioma a otro" (pp. 236–237). Both books are unread here; their wording is Jouhaud's quotation in Spanish translation.

sources.title: Roger Chartier, « La nouvelle histoire culturelle existe-t-elle ? », Les Cahiers du Centre de Recherches Historiques 31 (2003), online 15 September 2008.
sources.citation: Roger Chartier, « La nouvelle histoire culturelle existe-t-elle ? », Les Cahiers du Centre de Recherches Historiques 31 (2003), online 15 September 2008.

verification.note: Read in full for revision 1.147 in the OpenEdition HTML (paragraphs 1–31 and notes; no print pagination, so paragraphs are cited). ¶1: the category entered historians' common vocabulary when Lynn Hunt published her 1989 volume. ¶11: the critique of mentalités "était peut-être injuste"; shared demands: individual uses over statistical distributions, "les modalités spécifiques de leur appropriation", representations of the social world as constitutive of differences and struggles. ¶12: the risk of "une définition impérialiste de la catégorie". ¶19: forms "participent, elles aussi, à la construction de leur signification". ¶24: "C'est dans cet écart que s'insinuent reformulations et détournements, appropriations et résistances." ¶25: the linguistic turn holds "que la « réalité » n'est pas une référence objective, extérieure au discours"; against it, the logic of discourses and the logic of conduct are not identical; historians can rely on Foucault's distinction between "« formations discursives » et « systèmes non discursifs »" (n. 25) and Bourdieu's between "« sens pratique » et « raison scolastique »" (n. 26, Méditations pascaliennes, 1997); n. 24 cites Keith Baker for the linguistic-turn position. ¶26: social positions "ne sont pas seulement un effet des discours ; elles en désignent également les conditions de possibilité." ¶28: representation "en est presque venu à désigner en lui-même la nouvelle histoire culturelle". ¶31: "La cohérence la new cultural history est-elle aussi forte que le proclamait Lynn Hunt ? La diversité … permet d'en douter"; the field is defined "par l'espace d'échanges et de débats" among historians who refuse to reduce phenomena to one dimension and "se sont éloignés tant des illusions du tournant linguistique que des héritages contraignants qui postulaient le primat du politique ou la toute-puissance du social." Hayden White is not named. Also published in Francia 33/2 (2006), not read in that form.
